correctness.rationale: The two-world exchange formula Q(p)=((p→□p)→◇p)∧((◇p→p)→□p) equals the value of p at the other world for both inequalities x≤y, x≥y and equality. Structural induction on formulas substitutes local/other-world values and collapses modal nesting to one. The Gödel min/max/residuum operations only select input values, 0 or 1 according to weak-order type, so the complete 4-point order-type grid yields an exhaustive 342 two-generator term closure, versus six one-generator terms. For each d, the selection recurrence t_{r+1}=t_r∨(t_r→□t_r) and induction on the boundary constants B_r prove a (2d+1)-world finite witness separating depth d+1 from every depth≤d formula. Independent term closure reproduced 342,6,16 exchange cases; finite d tests do not prove the unbounded claim.
residual_risks: The boundary-band induction depends on the one-variable, no additional truth constants and universal crisp S5 semantics; no claim of minimal witness size.
